name: The Offspring
label: Epitaph
lede: A $20,000 record, a janitor's day job and a KROQ DJ's hunch make Smash the best-selling independent-label album ever. Then the band walks out on the label that made it.

eras.title: Garage kids from Cypress
eras.text: Two friends, a riot at a Social Distortion show and a drummer headed for medicine start a Southern California club band with its own label and a debut that comes out on vinyl and cassette only.

years.h: A Social Distortion riot sends two Cypress friends into a garage
years.p: Bryan "Dexter" Holland and Greg Kriesel had been playing together in Cypress, California since 1983. After the riot at a Social Distortion show in 1984 they form Manic Subsidal with drummer James Lilja.

years.h: Noodles leaves Clowns of Death for Manic Subsidal
years.p: Guitarist Kevin "Noodles" Wasserman's first show with the band is in Santa Cruz, opening for White Flag and Scared Straight.

years.h: A new name and a first single on their own Black Label
years.p: "I'll Be Waiting" comes out on the band's own Black Label imprint. A demo tape the same year gets a good notice in Maximum Rocknroll.

years.h: Sixteen-year-old Ron Welty takes the drums from a future oncologist
years.p: James Lilja leaves in 1987 to pursue a medical career in oncology. Welty, 16, takes over the kit.

years.h: A debut on Nemesis that you can't buy on CD
years.p: Thom Wilson produces The Offspring in summer 1989 for Nemesis Records. It's vinyl and cassette only until the CD arrives in 1995.

eras.title: A 7-inch gets them into Epitaph
eras.text: The Baghdad EP, made with Thom Wilson, opens the door at Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph, and tours with Pennywise, Lunachicks and NOFX build the following.

years.h: The Baghdad EP gets them signed to Epitaph
years.p: Producer Thom Wilson records the EP, and [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]] signs the band to his Epitaph Records.

years.h: Ignition: the last record before everything changed
years.p: The band tours it across the U.S. with [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]] and Lunachicks, then in Europe with [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]]. It's a club-circuit punk record, and the last one made at that size.

eras.title: Smash
eras.text: A $20,000 record, a janitor's day job and one KROQ DJ's pick turn a small Epitaph band into the label's whole story. Smash goes on to be called the best-selling independent-label album ever.

years.h: Thom Wilson lives in a camper van while cutting Smash
years.p: The band records in 20 days at Track Record Studios in North Hollywood on a budget of about $20,000, taking discounted studio time when it opens up.
years.xp:
The day jobs were still real. Noodles was a janitor at Earl Warren Middle School near Disneyland, per Louder, and Greg K. worked in a print shop. Dexter Holland was studying at USC and, Rolling Stone says, was up until 5 AM finishing lyrics in the last days.

When Gurewitz heard the finished record, Louder reports, he told his wife: "Everything's changed. We're going to be rich."

years.h: Smash arrives April 8 with a skeleton on the cover
years.p: The lead single, "Come Out and Play", comes from Holland's drives through gang-hit parts of South L.A.

years.big: "I was still sweeping up after little kids"
yt: Come Out and Play, official video
years.h: Jed the Fish makes "Come Out and Play" KROQ's Catch of the Day
years.p: Heavy rotation follows and the song tops Billboard's Modern Rock chart. Noodles, still on the school custodial crew, quits in mid-June.
years.xp:
Noodles said the line to Rolling Stone while the album was climbing the charts. Epitaph's Brett Gurewitz had hired a professional plugger to push the single to radio, per Louder, and KROQ's heavy rotation did the rest.

The video cost about $5,000 and was shot in a friend's garage, with most of the money going on meat and beer for the barbecue at the end of the shoot. Wikipedia says the album went gold and platinum within about four months. "Self Esteem" and "Gotta Get Away" followed as singles.

years.h: Holland and Greg K. start a label of their own, Nitro
years.p: Nitro re-releases the 1989 debut and goes on to sign [[The Vandals|f54fc7c3-3a40-4f26-83cf-328d9b097e93]], Guttermouth, Jughead's Revenge and [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]].

years.h: Weezer and Quicksand dates take the band from clubs to arenas
years.p: Tours with Weezer, [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] and No Use for a Name, plus Japan and Australia's Big Day Out, move the band from clubs to theaters and arenas, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: Smash money and a contract fight
eras.text: The record that made an independent label rich sets up a fight over terms, and the band leaves for Columbia.

years.h: The Offspring leave Epitaph for Columbia
years.p: Their lawyer cites "fundamental reasons" and says Epitaph breached the contract. Epitaph keeps the back catalog and reissues remastered Ignition and Smash in 2008.

years.big: "we thought we deserved more than Brett was willing to give us"
q: I never wanted to sell my label to a major label.
years.h: Two years of haggling over Smash money
years.p: Noodles gives Rolling Stone the band's side. Gurewitz, whose label Smash had made rich, said he never wanted to sell it to a major.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone says the band felt its outsized contribution to Epitaph's revenue justified better terms. Looking back, Gurewitz said: "I wish I would never have said a disparaging word about the Offspring. And I wish that they had never done the same to me."

He also said he was heartbroken at the loss.

years.h: Ixnay on the Hombre sells well, but it isn't Smash Part Two
years.p: Holland acknowledged that fans expected one. He directs the video for "I Choose" himself.

eras.title: Pretty Fly and the Napster summer
eras.text: Americana makes them a global pop act. The follow-up turns into a fight with their own label over free downloads.

yt: Why Don't You Get a Job?, official video
years.h: "Pretty Fly (for a White Guy)" tops the charts in nine countries
years.p: Americana spins off two more radio and MTV staples, "Why Don't You Get a Job?" and "The Kids Aren't Alright", and peaks at number two in the U.S., per Wikipedia.

yt: Pretty Fly (for a White Guy), the original video
years.h: Weird Al Yankovic answers with "Pretty Fly for a Rabbi"
years.p: [[Weird Al Yankovic|7746d775-9550-4360-b8d5-c37bd448ce01]] parodies the Americana single and swaps the poser for a rabbi.

yt: Come Out and Play, live at Woodstock '99
years.h: Idle Hands, then Woodstock '99
years.p: The band plays "I Wanna Be Sedated" and "Beheaded" in the movie Idle Hands and appears at Woodstock '99.

years.h: Sony threatens legal action, and the free album stays offline
years.p: The band wanted to put all of Conspiracy of One on its website. Only "Original Prankster" went up, and the rest leaked to fan sites.
years.xp: The band sold T-shirts with the Napster logo and gave the profits to Napster creator Shawn Fanning, per Wikipedia. Wikipedia says the threat came from Columbia through its parent, Sony. The album still went platinum.

years.h: Ron Welty leaves after 16 years, and the two stories differ
years.p: Welty said he left to join Steady Ground. Later reports said Holland and Noodles fired him without notice before the seventh album.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the firing to January 3, 2003, "without any prior notice." Josh Freese drummed on the Splinter sessions and Atom Willard, ex-Rocket from the Crypt, joined for touring.

Welty sued in 2020 over royalties from the $35 million catalog sale and lost in March 2023, when the judge called some of his claims "completely illogical."

years.h: Splinter puts electronic samples on "Hit That"
years.p: The seventh album is the last of the original Columbia deal, with Freese on drums.

eras.title: Stages get bigger, and Holland finishes a PhD
eras.text: The band settles into festival and amphitheater dates while its singer finishes a doctorate and the catalog changes hands.

years.cap: Dexter Holland and Atom Willard, Rock in Idro, Milan, September 2005
years.h: Greatest Hits, then the first Vans Warped Tour
years.p: The summer 2005 run follows the Greatest Hits collection. Drummer Atom Willard later joins Angels & Airwaves.

years.cap: The Offspring at Download Festival, June 2008
years.h: Eleven weeks at number one for "You're Gonna Go Far, Kid"
years.p: With producer Bob Rock behind the board, the single spends 11 weeks atop Hot Modern Rock Tracks, a record for the band.
play: Rise and Fall, Rage and Grace

years.h: Days Go By is cut with Bob Rock in Hawaii
years.p: Sessions begin in 2010 and the album comes out in June 2012.

years.cap: The Offspring at Sonisphere, Getafe, Spain, May 2012
years.h: Smash turns 20, and Bad Religion and Pennywise come along
years.p: A co-headline tour with [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]], Pennywise, [[The Vandals|f54fc7c3-3a40-4f26-83cf-328d9b097e93]], Stiff Little Fingers and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] celebrates the anniversary.
years.xp: The Summer Nationals EP covers Pennywise's "No Reason Why" and Bad Religion's "Do What You Want" and "No Control", per Wikipedia.

years.cap: The Offspring at Rock Allegiance, October 2016
years.h: Round Hill pays $35 million for the Columbia catalog
years.p: The band had reclaimed its Columbia albums in 2014 and auctioned them from 2015. Round Hill Music gets the catalog and the publishing.

years.cap: Dexter Holland and Todd Morse, Rock Allegiance, October 2016
years.h: Holland finishes a PhD in molecular biology at USC
years.p: It's the same university where he was a student during the Smash sessions.

eras.title: A co-founder out, a drummer out, a drummer back for one song
eras.text: Long-serving members leave through lawyers and public statements, and the band keeps touring and making records.

years.cap: The Offspring at Pinkpop, Netherlands, June 2018
years.h: Greg K. is out of the band he co-founded
years.p: Holland and Noodles told him he could no longer play or record with the band. Tony Kanal of No Doubt filled in for tours, and Todd Morse became the full-time bassist.
years.xp: Kriesel sued in August 2019, alleging that Holland and Wasserman had conspired to seize band assets. They countersued, saying he was asked and agreed to leave and that they tried to buy out his share. The case settled out of court in 2023, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Let the Bad Times Roll is the first album on Concord
years.p: It's released April 16 after a February announcement.

years.h: Pete Parada says he was fired over a vaccine
years.p: Parada said he was fired after declining a COVID-19 vaccine on his doctor's advice. Holland and Noodles said in November 2021 that they hired replacements for crew safety.

years.cap: The Offspring on Fremont Street, Las Vegas, February 2024
years.h: James Lilja plays "Beheaded" with the band for the first time in 36 years
years.p: Lilja, who co-wrote the song, sits in on August 6, 2023. Brandon Pertzborn had joined as permanent drummer in May.

years.cap: The Offspring at Rock en Seine, August 2024
years.h: Josh Freese leaves for Foo Fighters, and Brandon Pertzborn takes over
years.p: Freese replaces the late Taylor Hawkins. Pertzborn, formerly of Black Flag and Suicidal Tendencies, joins on May 12, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Supercharged follows the June single "Make It All Right"
years.p: The eleventh album comes out October 11 on Concord.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Smash, the little punk LP that defeated the majors
